subject: ichneumon wasp
title: This Wasp Drills Through Solid Wood With a Tail Thinner Than a Hair

scenes.text: A wasp drills solid wood for prey it cannot see.
The giant ichneumon wasp: two inches of body, then a hair-thin tail up to four inches long.
She presses her antennae to the bark and feels for vibrations: a horntail grub chewing tunnels inside the trunk.

scenes.text: Then she drills, usually about half an hour, through up to four inches of wood.
She paralyzes it and lays an egg. Her larva eats the grub alive, then flies out next spring to listen for another.

description:
A giant ichneumon wasp drills through solid wood with an egg-laying tube not much thicker than a horse hair.
The female is about two inches long with an ovipositor of two to four inches more. She presses her antennae to the bark to feel the vibrations of a horntail larva chewing inside, then drills, typically for about half an hour and sometimes for hours, through up to four inches of wood. She paralyzes the grub and lays an egg on it; her larva feeds on the living host and emerges the following spring.
Would you have guessed that tail was a drill?
first_comment: The tail looks like a giant stinger, but she can't sting you at all. Which insect weapon scares you more: a drill or a sting?
